Field.name: InputFile
Field.usage: Input file with image volume

Field.name: OutputFile
Field.usage: Output file for model of correlation peaks

Field.name: CandidateModel
Field.usage: Output model for initial points with highest pixel sums

Field.name: BeadSize
Field.usage: Size of beads in pixels
Field.manpage: Diameter of beads in pixels, a required entry. If the volume is binned, this size can be entered in unbinned pixels and the -binning entry used to specify the binning.

Field.name: BinningOfVolume
Field.usage: The current binning of the image volume, used to scale bead size
Field.manpage: The current binning of the image volume. The entered bead size is divided by this binning to obtain the actual size of the beads in the volume.

Field.name: ExpandedByFactor
Field.usage: Value of ExpandByFactor used in Newstack when making aligned stack
Field.manpage: Value of ExpandByFactor used in Newstack when making aligned stack, which will also be used to scale the binned bead size.

Field.name: XMinAndMax
Field.usage: Starting and ending X coordinates of region to find beads in
Field.manpage: Starting and ending X coordinates of region in which to find beads. X, Y, and Z coordinates are numbered from 1. The default is to search the whole volume.

Field.name: YMinAndMax
Field.usage: Starting and ending Y coordinates of region to find beads in

Field.name: ZMinAndMax
Field.usage: Starting and ending Z coordinates of region to find beads in

Field.name: LightBeads
Field.usage: Beads are light on dark background

Field.name: AngleRange
Field.usage: Starting and ending tilt angles, for computing elongation factor
Field.manpage: Starting and ending tilt angles, for computing the elongation factor due to the missing wedge in single-axis tomograpy. The elongation is computed using a formula in Radermacher (1988), with the maximum tilt angle for that formula taken as the mean of the absolute values of the minimum and maximum angles of the series. The elongation will be capped at 2.5, and the program will exit with an error if it exceeds 5.

Field.name: TiltFile
Field.usage: File with tilt angles, for computing elongation factor
Field.manpage: File with tilt angles, for computing elongation factor from the minimum and maximum tilt angle, as just described. Only one of -angle and -tilt may be entered.

Field.name: YAxisElongated
Field.usage: Features are elongated along the Y instead of Z axis
Field.manpage: Features are elongated by the missing wedge along the Y axis instead of the Z axis. This entry is needed when analyzing a tomogram as produced by Tilt(1) with Z slices along the tilt axis and Y perpendicular to the plane of the specimen.

Field.name: MinRelativeStrength
Field.usage: Minimum relative peak strength for retaining peak in analysis
Field.manpage: Minimum relative peak strength for keeping a peak in the analysis. The square root of the specified value is used for comparing with the square root of peak strength, for compatibility with existing command files. The default is 0.05, which corresponds to a relative square root peak strength of 0.22. Too many weak peaks can prevent a dip from showing up in the smoothed histogram of strengths. If the program fails to find a histogram dip, one strategy is to try raising this value.

Field.name: ThresholdForAveraging
Field.usage: Threshold relative peak strength or number of beads for averaging
Field.manpage: Threshold relative peak strength or number of beads for averaging. With a non-zero entry, selected beads from the first round of peak finding and integral measurement are averaged to produce a reference for a second round. If a negative value is entered, the program will analyze the histogram of peak strengths and find the dip indicating the best boundary between actual and false beads. The value has 4 different meanings depending on the range: ^ Greater than 1: an absolute number of beads with the strongest peaks ^ Between 0 and 1: minimum relative square root of peak strength ^ Between 0 and -1: negative of strongest fraction of peaks above histogram dip (e.g., -0.33 for the strongest 1/3 of the peaks above the dip) ^ -2: 1/4 of way from histogram dip to histogram peak (the default)

Field.name: StorageThreshold
Field.usage: Threshold relative peak strength for storing peaks in model
Field.manpage: Threshold relative peak strength for storing peaks in model. With a value of 0 (the default), the program will find the dip in the histogram of peak strengths, find the mean and SD of the strengths above the dip, and store all of the beads above the dip plus additional ones below the dip. The latter will be up to the 5 SD's below the mean or up to the number of ones above the dip. Enter a number between 0 and 1 to specify a relative square root strength above which peaks will be stored. Enter a negative number to specify the number to store as a fraction of the number above the histogram dip (e.g., -1 for all points above the dip, -0.33 for the strongest 1/3 above the dip, -1.33 for all above plus 1/3 that many below the dip.) If you use the default, or a number below -1, then you must examine the points in 3dmod, adjust the threshold if necessary, and delete points below the threshold.

Field.name: FallbackThresholds
Field.usage: Thresholds for averaging and storage if no histogram dip is found
Field.manpage: Thresholds to use as fallbacks when no histogram dip is found. The first number is a threshold to use for averaging when no dip is detected in the histogram of peak strengths in the first round. It can be between 0 and 1 to specify a relative peak strength, or a number greater than 1 to specify a number of beads. The second number is a threshold relative strength for peaks to store, between 0 and 1, when no dip is found in the histogram of second-round peak strengths. If a fallback is desired for only one of these two rounds, enter a zero for the other value.

Field.name: MinSpacing
Field.usage: Minimum spacing between peaks as fraction of bead size (default 0.9)
Field.manpage: Minimum spacing between peaks as a fraction of the bead size. When two peaks are closer than this distance apart, the weaker one is eliminated unless the -both option is entered. The default is 0.9. A value less than 1 is helpful for picking both beads in a pair.

Field.name: EliminateBoth
Field.usage: Eliminate both peaks when their spacing is below the minimum spacing

Field.name: GuessNumBeads
Field.usage: A guess for the number of beads, which can be an underestimate
Field.manpage: A guess for the number of beads. This entry may sometimes be required to help the program find a dip in the histogram, especially if there are very few beads. The number can be an underestimate and a very rough estimate. Use this entry if a histogram dip is found at a rather high peak strength with few peaks above it.

Field.name: MaxNumBeads
Field.usage: The maximum possible number of beads to look for
Field.manpage: The maximum possible number of beads to look for. Only this number of peaks will be retained and used for finding the histogram dip. If the program fails to find a histogram dip, try entering a value that is at least twice the estimated number of beads. The default is 50000.

Field.name: TemplateFile
Field.usage: File with volume to correlate with instead of average at pixel sum peaks

Field.name: CenterOfTemplateInXYZ
Field.usage: Center position from which to extract the template

Field.name: AnnulusRadii
Field.usage: Inner and outer radius of background annulus for 2D integrals

Field.name: TextOutputFile
Field.usage: Name for output text file for peak locations, strengths, CCCs, 2D integrals

Field.name: VerboseOutput
Field.usage: 1 for diagnostics, 2 for peaks, 3 and 4 for histogram verbosity
Field.manpage: Enter 1 for diagnostic output, 2 for listing of peaks, and 3 or 4 for verbose output from the histogram routines

Field.name: ParameterFile
Field.usage: Read parameter entries from file

Field.name: usage
Field.usage: Print help output
